Twelve verses, Medinan
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful
﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period and count the waiting period﴾
﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women, divorce them at their waiting period and count the waiting period﴾

As for its connection with what precedes it: Allah, exalted is He, said at the beginning of that surah: ﴿To Him belongs dominion, and to Him belongs praise, and He is over all things competent﴾ [at-Taghabun: 1]. Dominion requires disposition in a manner through which the order of the kingdom is achieved, and praise requires that this disposition be by way of justice and beneficence toward the one disposed of, and with the power to restrain whoever would prevent it from disposing. The establishment of rulings in this surah includes these matters that require them, in an inclusion that does not require reflection upon it. Thus this surah has a relation to that surah. As for the first in relation to the last: He, exalted is He, indicated at the end of that surah to the completeness of His knowledge with His saying: ﴿Knower of the unseen﴾ [at-Taghabun: 18], and at the beginning of this surah to the completeness of His knowledge of the interests of women and the rulings specific to their divorce. So it is as if He explained that universal through these particulars. As for His saying: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾, Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, narrated that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ divorced Hafsah, and she went to her family, and it was revealed. It was also said: he took her back, for she was fasting often and standing in prayer often. On this view, the verse was revealed only because of her going out to her family when the Prophet ﷺ divorced her, and Allah revealed in this verse: (and they should not leave) their houses. Al-Kalbi said: he, peace be upon him, became angry with Hafsah when he confided a matter to her and she disclosed it to Aisha, so he divorced her with a single divorce, and it was revealed. As-Suddi said: it was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Umar when he divorced his wife while she was menstruating, and the story concerning that is well known. Muqatil said: men did the same as Ibn Umar did, namely Amr ibn Sa'id ibn al-As and Utbah ibn Ghazwan, and it was revealed concerning them. Regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O Prophet, when you divorce women﴾, there are two aspects:
The first: He addressed the Prophet ﷺ and then addressed his community, because he is their master and exemplar; when he is addressed with the plural address, his community is included in that address. Abu Ishaq said: this is an address to the Prophet, peace be upon him, and the believers are included with him in the address.
The second: the meaning is "O Prophet, say to them: when you divorce women," so the saying is omitted. Al-Farra' said: He addressed him and made the ruling apply to all, as you say to a man: "Woe to you, do you not fear Allah? Do you not feel shame?", going to him and to the people of his household. And ﴿when you divorce﴾ means when you intend to divorce, as in His saying: ﴿when you rise to the prayer﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6], meaning when you intend the prayer, and the discussion of this has passed. As for His saying, exalted is He: ﴿so divorce them at their waiting period﴾, Abdullah said: when a man wants to divorce his wife, he divorces her while she is in a state of purity without having had intercourse. This is the view of Mujahid, Ikrimah, Muqatil and al-Hasan. They said: Allah, exalted is He, commanded the husband to divorce his wife, when he wishes divorce, during a purity in which he has not had intercourse with her, and this is His saying: ﴿at their waiting period﴾, meaning at the time of their waiting period, which is the purity by the consensus of the community. It was also said: for the sake of making their waiting period manifest. A group of the exegetes said: divorce for the waiting period means that he divorces her while she is pure and without intercourse. In sum, divorce during a state of purity is obligatory, otherwise the divorce would not be sunni (in accordance with the Sunnah). Divorce in accordance with the Sunnah is conceivable only for a woman who has reached puberty, has been consummated, is not past menopause, and is not pregnant, since there is no Sunnah (in accordance with the Sunnah) for a young girl, one not consummated, one past menopause, or one pregnant, and likewise there is no bid'ah (innovation) because of the absence of a waiting period by menstrual cycles. There is no Sunnah or bid'ah in the number of divorces according to the school of al-Shafi'i, so that if he divorces her three times during a valid purity, this is not innovative, unlike what the people of Iraq held, for they said: the Sunnah regarding the number of divorces is that he divorces with each single divorce during a valid purity. The author of an-Nazm said: "so divorce them at their waiting period" is a description of how the divorce is to be, and this lam (preposition) comes for various meanings, its basic sense being possession, and for indicating cause and reason, as in His saying: ﴿We feed you only for the sake of Allah's countenance﴾ [al-Insan: 9], and in the sense of "at" (ʿinda), as in His saying: ﴿Establish the prayer at the decline of the sun﴾ [al-Isra': 78], meaning at it, and in the sense of "in" (fi), as in His saying: ﴿It is He who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering﴾ [al-Hashr: 2]. In this verse it bears this meaning, because the meaning is "divorce them in their waiting period," that is, in the time that is suitable for their waiting period. The author of al-Kashshaf said: "divorce them" [coming at the start], "at their waiting period," as in His saying: "I came to him for a night that remained of Muharram," meaning, facing it. "In the recitation of the Prophet ﷺ: 'at the beginning of their waiting period'" So when a woman is divorced during the purity preceding her first menstrual period from her periods, she has been divorced at the start of her waiting period. The intent is that he divorces them during a purity in which they have not had intercourse, and they are left until their waiting period ends. This is the best divorce, the most fitting for the Sunnah, and the furthest from regret. This is supported by what is reported from Ibrahim an-Nakha'i that the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to prefer that they not divorce their wives in accordance with the Sunnah except with one divorce, and then not divorce otherwise until the waiting period ends, and that three divorces were considered base by them. Malik ibn Anas said: I know of no divorce except a single one, and he disliked three, whether combined or separated. As for Abu Hanifah and his companions, they disliked only what exceeds one divorce in a single purity. And it is narrated that the Prophet ﷺ said to Ibn Umar when he divorced his wife while she was menstruating: "This is not what Allah, exalted is He, commanded you. The Sunnah is that you await a purity deliberately, and divorce her once for each period." According to al-Shafi'i there is no harm in sending three divorces, and he said: I know of no Sunnah or bid'ah in the number of divorces, and it is permissible.
So Malik observes in the divorce of the Sunnah the single divorce and the time; Abu Hanifah observes the separation and the time; al-Shafi'i observes the time alone. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and count the waiting period﴾ means their periods; so guard them, and safeguard the rights and rulings that are due during the waiting period, and safeguard the very thing by which they count, which is the number of menstrual periods. Then entrusting the counting to the husbands admits of two aspects:
The first: they are the ones upon whom the rights and maintenance are obligatory.
The second: so that the protection of the children within the waiting period may be secured. Then there are several discussions in the verse:
The first: What is the wisdom in calling one divorce "sunni" and another "bid'i"? We say: it is called bid'ah because if she is menstruating, she has not counted her days of menstruation toward her waiting period, but the waiting period extends beyond three periods, so the waiting period becomes long for her until it is as if it were four periods, and she is in the menstruation during which she was divorced, in the form of one left in suspense, neither under waiting nor with a husband, and reason finds harm abhorrent. And if she is pure but has been had intercourse with, it cannot be ruled out that she has conceived a child from that intercourse, and had the husband known, he would not have divorced her. This is because a man may desire to divorce his wife when there is no child between them, and does not desire it when she is pregnant by him with a child. So if he divorces her while she has been had intercourse with and he believes that she is barren in outward appearance, and then a pregnancy appears in her, he regrets her divorce. So in divorcing her during menstruation there is ill regard for the woman, and in divorcing her during the purity in which he had intercourse with her, when she has conceived in it, there is ill regard for the husband. But when she is divorced while pure and not had intercourse with, these two matters are secured, because she begins her waiting period immediately after his divorce of her, and so it proceeds through three periods, and the man too is, outwardly, secure from her carrying a child by him.
The second: Does a divorce contrary to the Sunnah take effect? We say: yes, and he is sinful, because of what is reported from the Prophet ﷺ: "A man divorced his wife three times in front of him, and he said to him: 'Do you play with the Book of Allah while I am still among you?'"
The third: How is one divorced in accordance with the Sunnah when she does not menstruate, due to youth or old age or other reasons? We say: the young girl, the woman past menopause, and the pregnant woman are all, according to Abu Hanifah and Abu Yusuf, to have the three divorces separated over months. Muhammad and Zufar said: one does not divorce in accordance with the Sunnah except with a single divorce. As for one not consummated, she is not divorced in accordance with the Sunnah except with a single divorce, and the time is not observed.
The fourth: Is it disliked to divorce a consummated woman with a single irrevocable divorce? We say: the narration on this from our companions differs, and the apparent view is that it is disliked.
The fifth: "When you divorce women" is general, encompassing those who have been consummated and those who have not, those with waiting periods by menstruation, those past menopause, the young, and the pregnant. How then can it be validly restricted to those with waiting periods and to those who have been consummated? We say: there is no generality here, nor is there specificity either. Rather, "women" is a generic noun for females of mankind, and this genericity is a meaning present in all of them and in some of them, so it is permissible that "women" be intended as this and that. When it is said: "so divorce them at their waiting period," it is known that it is applied to some of them, namely those consummated who observe waiting by menstruation. Thus al-Kashshaf mentions it.
* Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And fear Allah, your Lord. Do not expel them from their houses, nor let them leave, unless they commit a clear immorality. And those are the limits of Allah; and whoever transgresses the limits of Allah has certainly wronged himself. You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that a matter﴾.
His saying: ﴿And fear Allah﴾: Muqatil said: fear Allah, so do not disobey Him in what He has commanded you. ﴿Do not expel them﴾, meaning do not expel the women in waiting from the dwellings in which you used to reside with them before the divorce. If the dwellings were lent and then reclaimed, the husbands must arrange other dwellings, by purchase, by rent, or otherwise. And the wives too must not leave, as a right of Allah, exalted is He, except for a manifest necessity; if she goes out by night or by day, that going out is forbidden, and the waiting period is not terminated.
His saying, exalted is He: ﴿unless they commit a clear immorality﴾: Ibn Abbas said: it is that they commit fornication, so they go out to have the prescribed punishment carried out upon them. Ad-Dahhak and most of the scholars said: the immorality on this view is adultery. Ibn Umar said: the immorality is their going out before the end of the waiting period. As-Suddi and the rest said: the clear immorality is manifest disobedience, namely nushuz (rebelliousness). It is also reported from Ibn Abbas: "unless they use abusive speech," so it becomes lawful to expel them because of their abuse and bad character, and it becomes lawful for husbands to expel them from their houses. Regarding the verse there are several discussions:
The first discussion: Is it permissible for the spouses to agree to waive it?

We say: The obligatory residence (al-sukna) while the marriage is intact is a right of the woman alone, so she may waive it. The reasoning is that while the spouses remain bound by the marriage, its purpose is companionship and enjoyment. For this to be complete, the woman must be ready for him whenever he needs her, and this can only be ensured if he provides for her maintenance (al-nafaqa): her food, drink, condiments, clothing, and residence. All of these are among the means by which the enjoyment described above is fully realized. Beyond this lies the right to guard the seed (siyanat al-ma'), and similar matters. If separation occurs, the basis that was the enjoyment disappears, and so does the means that led to it, namely the maintenance she is owed. The need to guard the seed remains, so the residence in this situation becomes obligatory because it is one of the means of that guarding, since its root is residence, as it is by residence that she is protected. In this situation, residence is no longer exclusive to the husband. Guarding the seed is one of the rights of Allah, and it is not permissible for the spouses to agree to waive it. Therefore she may not leave the residence even if the husband consents, nor may he expel her even if she consents, except out of necessity, such as the collapse of the house, a usurper expelling her, a move from a rented house whose lease has expired, fear of strife, flood, fire, or any other threat to her life. When the reason for her removal ends, she returns to her original place.

The second point: He said, ﴿Fear Allah, your Lord﴾, and did not say "Fear Allah" alone.

We say: This contains an emphasis that the other wording lacks. The word "Lord" (rabb) alerts them to the fact that the nurturing (tarbiya), which is bestowing favour and honour in many forms, is endless in its multiplicity. Therefore they will strive harder in piety out of fear of losing that nurturing.

The third point: What is the meaning of combining "their expelling" (ikhrajihim) with "their leaving" (khurujihinna)?

We say: The meaning of "expelling" is that the husbands should not drive them out in anger or out of dislike of their living with them, or out of their own need for the dwellings. It also means that they should not grant them permission to leave when they ask for it, signifying that their permission has no effect in lifting the prohibition. Nor should the women leave by themselves if they wish to do so.

The fourth point: It is recited as ﴿bi-fahisha mubayyina﴾ and ﴿mubayyana﴾. Whoever reads mubayyina with a kasra means that the very nature of the indecency, when one reflects upon it, becomes clear that it is indecency. Whoever reads mubayyana with a fatha means that it is demonstrated by proofs and made manifest by evidence. As for His saying ﴿And these are the limits of Allah﴾: the limits (hudud) are the barriers against transgressing, like the prohibitions. The limit in reality is the final point at which a thing ends. Muqatil said: what has been mentioned, the divorce of the Sunna (talaq al-sunna) and the rulings that follow it, returns to the matter, ﴿And whoever transgresses the limits of Allah﴾. This is a severe warning against whoever transgresses the divorce of the Sunna and whoever divorces outside of the waiting period ('idda), ﴿then he has wronged himself﴾, meaning he has harmed himself. It is not far-fetched that the meaning is: whoever oversteps the boundary which Allah the Exalted has set has placed himself in a position where his Lord did not place him. Wronging (zulm) is placing a thing in other than its proper place. As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿You do not know; perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾, Ibn Abbas said: it refers to regret over divorcing her and the desire to take her back during the waiting period. This is evidence that it is preferable for divorce to be pronounced in separate instances. Abu Ishaq said: if he divorces her three times at one time, there is no sense in His saying, ﴿perhaps Allah will bring about after that some matter﴾.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 65, verses 2–3:

﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a measure for everything.﴾

* * *

Then the Exalted said: ﴿So when they have reached their term, either retain them in good manner or part from them in good manner. And bring to witness two just men from among you and establish the testimony for Allah. That is instructed to whoever should believe in Allah and the Last Day. And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out.﴾ ﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect. And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him. Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose. Allah has already set a measure for everything.﴾

﴿When they have reached their term﴾: that is, they have come close to the end of the ʿiddah (the waiting period), not the end of their term itself. The meaning of "reaching the term" here is approaching the reaching, and its explanation has already passed. The author of al-Kashshaf (al-Zamakhshari) said: it is the end of the ʿiddah and its approach. So you have the choice: if you wish, then take her back and retain her in good manner (rajʿah, i.e. revocation of divorce), and if you wish, then leave off taking her back and part from her, but do not leave her in harm, which is that one takes her back at the end of the ʿiddah and then divorces her again, prolonging the ʿiddah and tormenting her.

As for His saying: ﴿And bring to witness two just men from among you﴾: that is, they were commanded to call upon two just men as witnesses at the time of divorce and at the time of revocation. This calling to witness is recommended according to Abu Hanifa, as in His saying: ﴿And call witnesses when you conclude a sale﴾ (al-Baqarah: 282). According to al-Shafiʿi, it is obligatory in revocation and recommended in separation. It has been said: the benefit of calling witnesses is that there is no denial between them, that he is not accused of retaining her, and so that if one of them dies, the survivor does not claim the continuation of the marriage in order to inherit. It has also been said: the calling of witnesses was commanded for precaution, lest the woman deny the revocation, so that the ʿiddah ends and she marries another husband. Then He addressed the witnesses, saying: ﴿and establish the testimony﴾. This too has already had its explanation.

As for His saying: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾: al-Shaʿbi said: whoever divorces for the ʿiddah, Allah will make for him a path to revocation. Others said: a way out of every matter that becomes narrow for people. al-Kalbi said: whoever is patient in calamity, Allah will make for him a way out from the Fire to Paradise. The Prophet (ﷺ) recited it and said: "A way out from the doubts of this world, and from the agonies of death, and from the hardships of the Day of Resurrection." Most of the exegetes said: "This and what follows it was revealed concerning ʿAwf ibn Malik al-Ashjaʿi, whose son was taken captive by the enemy. He came to the Prophet (ﷺ), told him of that, and complained to him of poverty. He said to him: 'Fear Allah, be patient, and recite much: there is no power and no strength except with Allah.' The man did so, and while he was in his house, his son came to him, the enemy having neglected him; he had seized camels and brought them to his father." The author of al-Kashshaf said: while he was in his house, his son knocked on the door with a hundred camels which the enemy had neglected and which he had driven off. That is His saying: ﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾. It is also possible that if he fears Allah and prefers what is lawful and patience with his family, Allah opens for him if he is in straitened circumstances: ﴿And He will provide for him from where he does not expect﴾. And he said in al-Kashshaf: ﴿And whoever fears Allah﴾ is a parenthetical clause emphasizing what preceded, namely the conduct of divorce according to the Sunnah, as has passed.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾: that is, whoever trusts in Him regarding what he attains, Allah suffices him in what concerns him. For this reason the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever wishes to be the strongest of people, let him rely upon Allah." It was read: ﴿Indeed, Allah will accomplish His purpose﴾ with the genitive construction (bālighu amrihi), and also (bālighun amrahu), meaning: carrying out His command. al-Mufaddal read (bālighan amrahu), with ﴿has already set﴾ being the predicate of "inna" and "bāligan" being a circumstantial accusative (ḥāl). Ibn ʿAbbas said: he means over all His creation. The meaning is: Allah will bring about His command regarding what He wills from you. And ﴿Allah has already set a measure for everything﴾: that is, a determination and a fixed time. This is an explanation of the obligation to rely upon Allah, the Exalted, and to entrust the matter to Him. al-Kalbi and Muqatil said: for everything, whether hardship or ease, there is a term at which it ends; Allah, the Exalted, has determined all of that, not to be advanced or delayed. Ibn ʿAbbas said: he means, "I determined what I created by My will."

[Page 32]

And His saying: ﴿When they have reached their term﴾ up to His saying: ﴿a way out﴾ is one verse; and from it up to His saying: ﴿a measure﴾ is another verse according to most scholars, while according to the Kufan and the Madinan (readers) the whole is one verse. Then in this verse there is a subtle point: that fear of Allah in caring for the affairs of women requires wealth. So the Exalted said: ﴿And whoever fears Allah – He will make for him a way out﴾. Close to this is His saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾ (al-Nur: 32). If it is said: ﴿And whoever relies upon Allah, then He is sufficient for him﴾ indicates there is no need for earning in seeking provision, while the saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾ (al-Jumuʿah: 10) indicates need, so how is that? We say: it does not indicate need, because His saying: ﴿disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah﴾ is for permissibility, as has passed, and permissibility is among things that contradict the need for earning, since need is incompatible with choice.

Commentary of al-Razi (Mafatih al-Ghayb) on surah 65, verse 4–5:

Then the Exalted said: ﴿And those of your women who have despaired of menstruation, if you are in doubt, their waiting period is three months, and those who have not menstruated [likewise]. And for those who are pregnant, their term is until they give birth to their load. And whoever fears Allah, He will make for him ease in his affair.﴾ ﴿That is the command of Allah, which He has sent down to you. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever believes in God and does righteous deeds, He will admit him into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein forever. God has certainly perfected provision for him﴾ ﴿God is the One who created seven heavens and of the earth their like. The command descends among them, so that you may know that God is capable of all things and that God has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾.

His saying: ﴿And whoever believes in God﴾ carries the meaning of wonder and glorification of what God has granted the believer of reward. It is read ﴿yudkhilhu﴾ with the ya' and with the nun. As for ﴿God has certainly perfected provision for him﴾, al-Zajjaj said: God has provided him with the Garden, whose bliss does not end. It was also said: ﴿rizqan﴾ means obedience in this world and reward in the Hereafter. Its parallel is ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ (al-Baqarah: 201).

Al-Kalbi said: He created seven heavens, some above others, like a dome. And of the earth, their like in being layers closely joined together. This is the well-known view that the earth consists of three layers: a purely earthy layer, a clayey layer which is not purely earthy, and a layer exposed, part of it in the sea and part of it on land, which is the inhabited world. There is nothing far-fetched in His saying ﴿and of the earth their like﴾ regarding it being seven climes according to the seven heavens, and the seven planets within them, which are the wandering stars. For each of these planets has properties whose effects appear in each clime of the earth, and thus they become seven in this respect. These are the aspects which reason does not reject. As for the other aspects transmitted from the people of tafsir (exegesis), those are among the things which reason rejects, such as the saying that the seven heavens are: the first a surging, restrained wave; the second stone; the third iron; the fourth copper; the fifth silver; the sixth gold; and the seventh ruby. And the saying of one who says: between each of them is a journey of five hundred years, and the thickness of each of them is likewise, is not considered valid by the people of tahqiq (verification), unless it was transmitted mutawatir (through widely attested, successive chains). It is possible that it is more than that, and God knows best what it is and how it is.

His saying: ﴿God is the One who created﴾ is a mubtada' (subject) and khabar (predicate). ﴿Mithlahunna﴾ is read in the accusative, coordinated with ﴿seven heavens﴾, and in the nominative, as a mubtada' whose khabar is ﴿and of the earth﴾.

His exalted saying: ﴿The command descends among them﴾. Ata said: it means the revelation among them to His creation in every earth and every heaven. Muqatil said: it means the revelation from the highest heaven to the lowest earth. Mujahid said: ﴿The command descends among them﴾ means with the life of some and the death of others, the safety of this and the destruction of that, as an example. Qatadah said: in every heaven of His heavens and every earth of His earths there is a creation of His creation, a command of His command, and a decree of His decree. It is also read ﴿yanzilu al-amr baynahunna﴾.

His exalted saying: ﴿so that you may know that God is capable of all things﴾. It is read ﴿li-ya'lamu﴾ with the ya' and the ta', meaning: so that you may know, when you reflect upon the creation of the heavens and the earth and the governance that operates in them, that whoever's power has reached this extent, which cannot belong to anyone else, his power is essential, and nothing frustrates him in what He wills. His saying ﴿that God is capable of all things﴾ is due to what was mentioned before. ﴿And that God has encompassed all things in knowledge﴾ means: all things, universal and particular, nothing escapes His knowledge, not the weight of an atom in the earth or in the heaven. He knows all things and is capable of bringing into being after annihilation. So blessed is God, Lord of the worlds. There is no power and no strength except with God, the Most High, the Mighty. And prayers and peace be upon our master Muhammad, the master of the messengers, the leader of the God-fearing, and the seal of the prophets, and upon his family and all his companions.
